evidence.source: Academia Sinica Institute of History and Philology, Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The character-specific record lists oracle-bone script, bronze inscriptions (including 集成06305), Chu manuscripts, small seal script, and Shuowen. The browser exposed labels and an inscription reference, but not the glyph images; this record supports the sequence of catalogued form categories, not detailed visual claims about their strokes.
evidence.title: 漢字「行」：字形演變

evidence.source: Guo Lihua, Fudan University Center for Research on Excavated Texts and Ancient Chinese Characters
evidence.field: Oracle-bone 行; cited examples 屯2178 and 合集24391
evidence.text: Guo reads the oracle-bone graph as a crossroads and argues that its original graphic sense was ‘road’; she cites oracle-bone contexts meaning ‘meet on the road’ and ‘a rhinoceros is on the road.’ She proposes the semantic direction road → walking/go, an interpretation rather than a chronology established by the graph alone.
evidence.title: 郭麗華：《甲骨文字典》釋義補正五則

evidence.source: Chi-hsiung Cheng et al., University of Chicago Center for East Asian Studies archive
evidence.field: §2 graphic analysis and usage, PDF pp. 4–5
evidence.text: The authors describe oracle-bone forms as four-way thoroughfares; they report an upper stroke variation in one example and say Western Zhou bronze forms continue the oracle-bone shape. They cite oracle-bone verbal uses, including 21901, 24445, and 33033, as well as later movement and Warring States conduct examples. They also state that the graph’s road-like form cannot by itself order the spoken senses.
evidence.title: 「行」字意義的變遷

evidence.source: Chi-hsiung Cheng et al., University of Chicago Center for East Asian Studies archive
evidence.field: §3 sound and meaning analysis, PDF pp. 6–8
evidence.text: The authors report Guangyun categories 胡郎切 (row/rank), 戶庚切 (walking/going), 下浪切 (order), and 下更切 (conduct/action). They hypothesize relations among the senses and readings, but label proposed chronology as inference and say the Jingdian Shiwen evidence is inconclusive. Their Sino-Tibetan comparisons are presented as debated proposals.
evidence.title: 「行」字意義的變遷

evidence.source: Xu Shen, Shuowen Jiezi, online transcription
evidence.text: The entry says 人之步趨也 and analyzes the graph as 从彳从亍. This is a Han-era lexicographic account of walking and graph structure. It does not independently establish that the oracle-bone graph originated as a compound of the two modern-looking parts.
evidence.title: 說文解字「行」

gaps: The Sinica evolution page exposed script labels and an inscription citation but not glyph images; detailed stroke-by-stroke development and possible corruption remain unverified.

Scholars disagree on whether road or walking/go came first as a spoken sense. The graph depicts a thoroughfare, while the cited verbal oracle-bone uses already attest movement; graph shape does not resolve lexical chronology.

No component is proposed: 彳 and 亍 are discussed only as parts in the later Shuowen analysis, not established here as original semantic or phonetic components. The possible whole-graph loan account from the dossier is not independently supported by inspected sources; no sound match or source-word chronology was established.
The Shuowen transcription page could not be read by the browser in this pass. The dossier supplies the Han-era passage but it is not newly externally verified here.
Official Unihan page for 行 was inaccessible, so current Mandarin reading is carried only as a supplied local row, not as externally verified evidence.

limitations.text: Did not select a Shang oracle-bone image: although Commons lists an oracle-script version as a related file, this pass did not inspect its exact description page and provenance. The chosen seal image alone cannot illustrate the earliest graphic form.
